subject: Clarify billable streaming policy and commit slab smoothing
messages:
From: Maya R. <maya@datagforge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@datagorge.com>, procurement@datagorge.com
Date: 2026-10-15T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API billing questions — streaming & commit tiers

Thanks Kimberly — the team looked over the proposed pricing and we have a couple of open items that need explicit contract language before procurement can sign: 

1) How are streaming responses billed when a client terminates the stream mid-response? We saw different language in the term-sheet and want to avoid surprise credits or debits at month end.
2) Your commit tiers spreadsheet shows "slab smoothing" — can you explain how unused commit in a slab carries forward, if at all?

We're attaching a short note and a redline of the term-sheet with our suggested wording. Can you loop in legal/finance if needed?

— Maya
Procurement, DataForge

Attachment: DF_request_note.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya@datagforge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API billing questions — streaming & commit tiers

Hi Maya — thanks for the fast review and the redline. High-level answers here and I attached a proposal spreadsheet that maps the math to examples: commit-slab-proposal-v2.xlsx. More detailed legal wording below.

1) Streaming mid-response: our billing unit is "billable token" which counts tokens emitted by the model plus input tokens. For streaming responses terminated by the client, we bill for tokens actually emitted up to termination. There is no rounding up to the next full chunk by default — we meter at token granularity. However, for very short bursts (<= 4 tokens) we can apply a micro-billing floor in the contract to avoid noise; we are proposing a 4-token micro-floor in the draft term-sheet.

2) Slab smoothing / carry-forward: the default commit tiers operate on a monthly basis with a one-month smoothing window. That means if you commit 1.5B tokens/month and use 1.2B in month 1, the 0.3B surplus can be applied to the following month within the smoothing window. Unused tokens beyond that window do not convert to credits. We can negotiate longer smoothing windows for multi-year deals; see the attached commit-slab spreadsheet for example math.

Action items: 
- Marcus: please confirm micro-floor token value and whether we expose an opt-out in the contract.
- Aditya: confirm streaming-metering wording for legal (I drafted language below).

Best,
Kimberly
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: commit-slab-proposal-v2.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API billing questions — streaming & commit tiers

Kimberly — micro-floor sounds fine operationally. We usually set that at 4 tokens for network/processing overhead; billing will aggregate at the token level in the metering pipeline so the floor is only an invoice presentation convenience. Opt-out is fine but we should limit opt-out to enterprise-grade customers who take reserved capacity (Dedicated) — otherwise the micro-noise creates too many small invoice line-items.

I'll mark that in the proposal and add a note that opt-out requires a dedicated capacity clause.

— Marcus
Head of Pricing Operations

(Attachment: commit-slab-proposal-v2.xlsx - updated tab: micro-floor notes)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Maya R. <maya@datagforge.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API billing questions — streaming & commit tiers

Maya / Kimberly — legal-friendly wording below that I suggest we include in the term-sheet under "Usage Metrics & Billing":

"Billable Unit. 'Billable Token' shall mean a unit of metering equal to one token as counted by Redwood's metering service, where tokens include input tokens, prompt tokens, and tokens emitted by a model in response. For streaming responses, Billable Tokens shall be counted up to the moment the customer explicitly terminates the stream or the stream otherwise ends. Billing will be calculated at token granularity; however, Redwood may apply a micro-billing floor of four (4) tokens per streaming request for invoice presentation purposes. Customers who commit to Dedicated capacity may request an exception to the micro-billing floor via a signed amendment."

Also added: "Commit Smoothing. Monthly committed token volumes shall be evaluated on a calendar month basis. Unused tokens may be carried forward into the immediately following calendar month (the 'Smoothing Window') for the purposes of satisfying committed volumes. Any unused tokens remaining after the Smoothing Window shall expire. Longer smoothing windows or cumulative true-ups may be negotiated for multi-year agreements and shall be documented in the applicable order form."

If that reads OK to DataForge, legal can accept that language as-is and we'll push a redline.

— Aditya
Applied ML / Metering

(Attachment: term-sheet-streaming-definition.docx)

From: Maya R. <maya@datagforge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-17T10:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API billing questions — streaming & commit tiers

Thanks — helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement: 
- For charge disputes we need an exportable monthly metering report that shows request IDs, timestamps, and token counts. Is that available?
- If we terminate a stream because of a client-side bug and later replay the request (resulting in duplicate tokens), how are duplicates handled? We worry about accidental double charges.

If you can answer those two items and accept the smoothing window as 1 month, procurement is prepared to move to legal redlines.

— Maya

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya@datagforge.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API billing questions — streaming & commit tiers

Maya — quick answers: 

1) Metering export: yes, we provide a monthly metering CSV (or programmatic S3/BigQuery export for enterprise) that includes request_id, timestamp, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and total_billable_tokens. For disputes, we accept a 45-day window to raise a billing inquiry.

2) Duplicate tokens / replay: by default each request_id is treated as independently billable. To avoid accidental duplicates, we support idempotency keys on the API; when customers supply an idempotency key, retries within a 24-hour window will not be double-billed. We'll include the idempotency behavior in the metering doc and the term-sheet.

Next steps: I will circulate a clean term-sheet with the agreed language (micro-floor, smoothing window = 1 month, idempotency note) and attach the redline for your legal team. If DataForge approves, we can move to signature and set the first-month commit true-up timeline.

Best — Kimberly

Attachments: DF_Redline_20261015.pdf
